card: Encodes -torpassword as unquoted hexadecimal when authenticating to the Tor control port instead of wrapping it in an escaped quoted string. Currently, passwords containing backslashes fail authentication or get mangled because Bitcoin Core only escapes double quotes while Tor parses backslash escape sequences. The Tor control specification explicitly permits hex-encoded tokens to avoid escaping issues, and this PR adds a functional test covering backslashes and quotes.
changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the approach or diff; patch ID updated from a minor rebase or formatting update.
evidence: PR description: 'The Tor password was sent as a QuotedString with only double quotes escaped; as Tor interprets backslash escapes inside it, any password containing a backslash was mangled (or left the string unterminated).'
The Tor control specification section 3.5 explicitly allows hex-encoded strings for authentication to avoid escaping issues.
problem: Tor control passwords containing backslashes fail authentication or get corrupted. Bitcoin Core previously wrapped the password in a quoted string and only escaped double-quote characters, causing Tor's control port parser to interpret backslashes as escape sequences or reject trailing backslashes as unterminated escapes.

risk.why: A bug in formatting the Tor authentication command would fail Tor control authentication on startup for nodes using password-protected Tor control ports.

summary: Sends the `-torpassword` argument hex-encoded in the Tor control port `AUTHENTICATE` command rather than as a double-quoted string with escaped quotes. It also adds a functional test verifying that passwords containing special characters such as backslashes and quotes successfully authenticate against a mock Tor control server.
